title: risk quarantine and hotfix pathways for llm rollouts (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft describing a standardized risk-quarantine and hotfix pathway for LLM feature rollouts (canaries, microreleases, and A/B experiments) across Redwood products. Focus: reduce blast radius for behavioral regressions, streamline human-in-the-loop decisioning, and shorten mean-time-to-repair for quality/latency/cost incidents caused by model changes or routing policies.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to staged rollouts initiated via Console or the rollout API (canary, staged exposure, traffic slices).
- Covers behavioral regressions (toxicity, hallucination spikes), latency/cost regressions (token burst, cold-KV-cache effects), and model-serving correctness (wrong tool calling, malformed structured responses).
- Excludes infra-only failures (node oom, disk full) except where they interact with model selection/routing.

High-level goals:
1) Contain a bad signal quickly to a quarantined cohort with minimal manual overhead.
2) Provide clear decision gates: rollback, hotfix, patch + continue, or degrade gracefully to fallback model.
3) Give oncall and product owners deterministic playbooks and templates for comms and postmortem.

Trigger signals (automated + human):
- Telemetry thresholds (examples):
  - toxic_score > baseline + 6 sigma over 1m window on canary slice
  - avg_generation_latency > SLO * 1.5 for >5m and error rate >2x
  - token-cost per request > 3x baseline for specific user cohorts
- Evaluations: automated prompt-suite regression tests failing >= 15% of control prompts on canary model
- Manual reports: CS or internal user flags from support slack channel #model-safety or #prod-alerts
- Observability anomalies: sudden KV cache miss rate increase, long tail latency spikes in per-token histogram

First response (containment) - automated pre-checklist (0-3 minutes):
- Abort further slice widening: freeze rollout via console API (automated guardrail).
- Create quarantine cohort: route new incoming requests matching the slice to a gated route (quarantine) that isolates traffic to a dedicated fallback or to 0% acceptance with synthetic ack.
- Raise alert to oncall with pre-populated template (see comms section).
- Snapshot model variant and runtime metrics (KV usage, batch sizes, worker heatmap).

Quarantine options (choose based on signal severity):
- Silent Quarantine (low-severity): divert 100% of canary traffic to fallback model variant with no UI change; monitor 30 minutes.
- Visible Quarantine (medium): show reduced functionality banner to internal-only cohorts or beta users; route traffic to degraded model or cached responses for repeated prompts.
- Hard Quarantine (high): cut exposure to 0% and revert traffic to last-known-good configuration; open high-priority incident.

Decision matrix (quick guide):
- If behavioral regression on safety metrics AND failing evaluation set -> immediate rollback to prior model variant and start hotfix lane.
- If latency/cost regression without safety concerns and can be mitigated by config (smaller max_tokens, batching adjustments) -> apply config hotfix, monitor 15 minutes, then consider resuming.
- If mixed signals (safety marginal + latency high) -> hard quarantine + deeper eval; schedule hotfix only after failing root-cause checks.

Hotfix lanes and owner handoffs:
1) Configuration hotfix (fast lane, target < 30m to apply):
   - Owners: runtime oncall + product steward
   - Actions: reduce model max_length, lower top_p, enable prefix cache, change batching policy; roll config via feature flag to canary slice only.
2) Model patch (medium lane, target < 4h):
   - Owners: applied-ml + model onboarding lead
   - Actions: revert to earlier quantization profile or model checkpoint; run regression eval locally + small synthetic replay; push variant to canary after green checks.
3) Model retrain or prompt/adapter tweak (long lane, > 24h):
   - Owners: research/applied-ml + product
   - Actions: collect failing prompts, create focused dataset, iterate on prompt templates/adapter, run targeted evals and safety review.

Operational runbook (checklist for oncall):
- Acknowledge alert and set incident severity within 5 minutes.
- Run automated diagnostic script: capture top-50 failing prompts, sample 100 request traces, collect worker and GPU heatmaps.
- Decide quarantine option and implement routing change (Console quick action or API): document time and actor in incident header.
- If applying configuration hotfix: record exact flag changes and ensure rollback flag present.
- Notify stakeholders via incident comms: product PM, SRE lead, CS oncall, support triage. Use template: "[INCIDENT] Canary risk quarantine: slice X -> diverted to fallback. Signal: <metric>. Action: <quarantine type>. ETA next update: 15m."
- After stabilization, run smoke eval on control and canary slices, and update incident with quantitative delta.

Rollback vs hotfix decision heuristics (quick):
- Rollback when: safety metrics exceed thresholds OR structured-output correctness broken OR must-fix business logic error.
- Hotfix when: regressions are confidently attributable to runtime/config change OR small prompt adapter fixes can be applied quickly.

Communication templates (for slack/email):
- Initial alert (short): "[INCIDENT][Canary] Slice: <slice-id>. Signal: <top-metric>. Action: quarantined -> routed to fallback. Owner: <oncall>. More: <incident-doc>"
- Internal update (15m): include metrics baseline vs current, top failing prompts, and next steps.
- Customer-facing status (only if customer-facing cohort impacted): short plain-language note and ETA for resolution; escalate to Customer Success.

Post-incident process and guardrail improvements:
- Triage immediately after incident closed: collect labeled failing prompts and add to a shared repro corpus (apply privacy filters).
- Run localized A/B replays on repro corpus before re-exposing traffic.
- Create follow-up tickets: permanent metric alarms, additional synthetic tests, console UX for one-click quarantine.
- Quarterly review: compute MTTR, false-positive quarantine rate, and benefit of each hotfix lane.

Example scenarios (short vignettes):
1) Safety spike from new model: automatic toxic_score alert triggered. Action: hard quarantine, immediate rollback, create model-patch ticket for applied-ml to update safety filters.
2) Token-cost regression during extended context: detected cost increase for long-conversation cohort. Action: silent quarantine + config hotfix to cap max_tokens for that slice; monitor cost deltas.
3) Tool-calling regression (structured output misrouted): visible quarantine + revert to previous tool-schema-enabled model; run adapter patch in medium lane.

Open questions / unresolved items (for this docs iteration):
- How should we version and share the quarantine cohort definition to downstream billing and analytics pipelines (so cost attribution remains accurate)?
- Should quarantine cohorts be automatically recreated with synthetic traffic for later offline debugging? Privacy implications?
- Level of automation: which signals can we trust to auto-trigger a hard quarantine versus requiring human confirmation?

Immediate next work items (who/what):
- Build console quick-action for "quarantine slice" (owner: console team, Marco Ruiz) - prototype by 2026-01-15.
- Add toxic_score and eval-failure as default canary alarms (owner: observability, Lina Chen) - ship smoke checks 2025-12-01.
- Create incident comms templates in PagerDuty/Slack integrations (owner: product ops, Priya Rao).

Appendix: useful commands and artifacts
- Diagnostic script location: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/diagnose-canary.sh (run with --slice-id).
- Example incident ticket: JIRA-RDWF-786 (linked above).

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this doc intentionally concise, point to more formal runbooks once stabilized.
- Plan a simulation/rehearsal with SRE/product in Q1 to validate the hard-quarantine flow.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Aisha).
- 2026-01-12: added decision matrix and hotfix lanes (Devon + Lina).
- 2026-03-10: clarified comms templates and added open questions (Marco + Priya).
